blocks.html: The main service interface for the Audit Module.

This method records one or more audit logs. Unlike other modules' create
methods, it returns nothing, never throws and never waits for storage: the audit logs are validated, given an ID, and buffered, then
written in batches by the module's default provider. An invalid audit log is
dropped and logged. When the module's `enabled` option is `false`, this
method does nothing.

children.name: action
children.description: The name of the action, such as `order.cancel`.

children.description: The ID of the Medusa staff member acting as the actor, on Medusa Cloud.

children.description: The type of resource acted on, such as `order`.

children.name: resource_id
children.description: The ID of the resource acted on.

children.name: outcome
children.description: How the action ended.

children.name: started_at
children.description: When the action started, as a `Date` or an ISO 8601 string.

children.name: ended_at
children.description: When the action ended, as a `Date` or an ISO 8601 string.

children.name: request
children.description: The HTTP details. Leave empty for an audit log written outside an API request.

children.name: method
children.description: The HTTP method, such as `POST`.

children.description: The route pattern, such as `/admin/orders/:id/cancel`.

children.name: request_id

children.description: The client IP address.

children.description: The client user agent.

children.name: request_data
children.description: The request fields to keep. Never pass a whole request body.

children.name: response_data
children.description: The response fields to keep. Never pass a whole response body.

children.name: metadata
children.description: Any other data to attach to the audit log.

blocks.html:
This method writes every buffered audit log through the default provider and
resolves once done. It never throws. The module calls it on shutdown; call it
yourself when you need recorded audit logs to be readable right away, such
as in a script that exits afterwards.
